title: Auditor Evidence Pocket Guide
summary: Compact reference for customer-facing audits: RBAC v2 overview, audit log schema snapshot, SIEM export mapping, and a pragmatic evidence automation checklist for questionnaire responses.
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, auditor-facing pocket guide intended for solutions engineers and security contacts who need a quick, defendable set of artifacts when responding to customer security questionnaires and live audits. Not exhaustive — links to canonical sources provided.

Audience:
- Solutions / Sales engineering during customer reviews
- Customer security reviewers and auditors
- Internal CS/systems engineers preparing evidence bundles

High-level notes (what to emphasize orally):
- RBAC v2: fine-grained roles, least-privilege by default, audit trails for role changes, time-bound temp roles for escalations.
- Audit logs: immutable append-only streams with integrity metadata, daily retention ring for hosted customers and configurable retention for Private deployments.
- SIEM export: standardized JSON lines, field mapping to customer SIEM (see sample mapping).
- Evidence automation: small scripts + signed bundles reduce turnaround time and human error.

1) RBAC v2 (short explainer):
- Model: role-based + attribute filters. Roles are the core grant objects (e.g., infra-admin, model-deploy, token-reader).
- Scopes: roles can be scoped by org, project, or workload tag. Default is org-scoped.
- Inheritance: support for linear inheritance only (no DAG complexity). We avoid multiple inheritance to keep audits simple.
- Principles to call out: least privilege, separation of duties, approval workflows for role creation, time-limited elevation (just-in-time).
- Evidence artifacts to attach: role catalog export (CSV), sample role binding audit (who/when/why), policy change PR and approval threads.

2) Audit log schema snapshot (concise):
- id: UUID (string)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- actor: {type, id, email}  -- flattened as actor_type, actor_id, actor_email
- action: string (e.g., "role.bind", "model.deploy", "key.rotate", "login.failed")
- resource_type: string (e.g., "model", "deployment", "key", "route")
- resource_id: string
- outcome: string (success|failure|partial)
- request_id: string (correlator for distributed traces)
- ip: client IP (v4/v6)
- user_agent: string
- meta: free-form JSON blob (stringified for export)
- signature: base64 (optional integrity field)

Quick sample (human-readable):
2025-02-05T15:21:08Z | actor_email=ops+alice@redwood.ai | action=role.bind | resource_type=org | resource_id=org-42 | outcome=success | request_id=req-1a2b3c | ip=35.190.12.8

Notes: we keep meta small in customer exports to avoid exposing internal traces. When asked for raw logs we provide a scoped export with an agreed timeframe and filtering.

3) SIEM export mapping (one-paragraph + fields):
- Format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). UTF-8, compressed with gzip if >50MB.
- Timestamp field: ts (ISO8601).
- Severity mapping: outcome -> severity (failure -> high, partial -> medium, success -> info).
- Mandatory fields in customer export: ts, actor_email (or actor_id where email suppressed), action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip, outcome.
- Optional: user_agent, meta (string), signature.

Example NDJSON line (single-line):
{"ts":"2025-02-05T15:21:08Z","actor_email":"ops+alice@redwood.ai","action":"role.bind","resource_type":"org","resource_id":"org-42","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-1a2b3c","ip":"35.190.12.8"}

4) Evidence automation snapshot (practical checklist / current plan + TODOs):
- Pipeline: query log store -> filter by timeframe & customer-id -> redact internal-only fields -> sign and bundle -> upload to secure customer share (S3 presigned link or customer SFTP).
- Tools: small Python CLI (evidence-export), a GitHub repo with templates (see linked PR), and a Lambda + Step Function for on-demand exports.
- Automation deliverables (MVP):
  * evidence-export CLI v0.1 (filter, redact, package) - in review (PR #47)
  * signed manifest (SHA256 + metadata)
  * audit-bundle format: {manifest.json, logs.ndjson.gz, roles.csv, approvals.pdf}
- Security controls: export runs under a dedicated service principal, ephemeral credentials, and export activity is itself logged in the audit stream.
- Customer Qs to expect: "Can you prove logs weren't altered?" -> provide manifest + signature and describe immutability policy + retention.

5) Suggested short answers for common questionnaire items (copyable):
- Q: "How do you enforce least privilege?"
  A: "RBAC v2 enforces least privilege by default: roles are minimal privileges, role bindings are scoped to org/project, and we require approval for privileged role creation. Temporary elevation is supported via time-limited grants and recorded in audit logs."
- Q: "What is your audit log retention?"
  A: "Hosted accounts: default 90 days with the option to enable extended retention. Dedicated/Private customers: configurable retention contracts per SLA; retention policies are documented per deployment."
- Q: "How do you deliver logs to our SIEM?"
  A: "We provide NDJSON exports (gzipped), a direct S3 push connector, or syslog/collector integration. Exports include agreed mandatory fields and an integrity manifest."

6) Packaging checklist for a customer deliverable (rapid prep):
- [ ] Confirm timeframe and scope with customer (timezone, start/end).
- [ ] Run evidence-export CLI with customer-id and timeframe flags.
- [ ] Redact internal-only fields (confirm pattern).
- [ ] Generate manifest.json and sign with support key.
- [ ] Upload bundle to agreed destination and share link + checksum.
- [ ] Create a short cover note: what’s included, canonical links, point-of-contact.

7) Sample cover note (template):
Subject: Audit log export for Acme Corp (2025-02-01 -> 2025-02-05)
Body: Attached is the export package as requested. The package includes logs.ndjson.gz, roles.csv, and a signed manifest. The manifest lists the SHA256 checksums and the export criteria. If you need a different timeframe or more fields, reply with the timeframe and we will regenerate the export.

8) Evidence provenance and acceptance criteria (for internal reviewers):
- Provenance: every bundle must reference the export job ID, operator, and PR that allowed any manual changes.
- Acceptance: logs parseable as NDJSON, manifest signature validates, roles.csv present and matches role-binding sample, approvals.pdf present for any privileged changes.

9) Things we should escalate to eng/research (open questions):
- Should audit logs include a protected integrity ledger (e.g., append-only Merkle root) for all customers? (SEC-312 touches this)
- Standardize meta field schema to reduce customer parsing burden.
- Decide on default export retention and packaging size limits.

10) Links & references (quick):
- RBAC v2 design (Confluence) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design+Notes
- Evidence export repo (GitHub PR) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/evidence-exports/pull/47
- Jira epic for export automation - https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-312

Notes to self (todo):
- Add a short appendix with an obfuscated example of a signed manifest.
- Coordinate with DevRel on a one-pager for customers who want SIEM onboarding help.
- Confirm legal's preferred text for evidence-sharing agreements.

-- end --
